# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

**This index is maintained by hand.** It previously said "auto-generated by the CI pipeline", which
was false: no workflow step, script or MSBuild target anywhere in this repository reads or writes
`docs/adr/`, and `docs/25-ADR.md` §14 still records "whether the index is regenerated by a tool or
hand-edited" as an *open deferred decision* (`ADR-D-2`). A file that claims to be generated is a file
nobody updates, which is how this index came to list one ADR while five documents cited four others.
Audit TD-40.

**What is enforced instead.** `DocumentStatusTests.EveryAdrCitedInSourceHasAFile` fails the build if
source code cites an `ADR-NNNN` with no corresponding file here. That is narrower than a generated
index and it is real.

| ADR | Title | Status | Closes OD |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-record-architecture-decisions.md) | Record architecture decisions | Accepted | — |
| [0012](0012-no-telemetry.md) | Pine collects no telemetry, and performs no network I/O at all | Accepted | OD-10 |
| [0013](0013-encryption-baseline.md) | Encryption baseline: SQLCipher at rest, Argon2id auth key, AES-256-GCM key envelope | Accepted | OD-03 |

## What is NOT here, and why that matters

`docs/25-ADR.md` §11 seeds **twenty** ADRs, `0001`–`0020`, and marks every one of them **Accepted**.
Seventeen of those twenty have no file. An "Accepted" decision with no record is not a decision that
was made and written down badly — it is a claim about the project's history that nothing supports.
Treat §11 as a *backlog of ADRs to write*, not as a register of decisions taken.

Two further defects in that register are recorded here so they are not rediscovered:

- **Two incompatible numbering schemes are in use.** `09-System-Architecture` §16,
  `19-Traceability-Matrix` and `10-Domain-Model` use a two-digit `ADR-01`…`ADR-10` scheme; `25-ADR`
  §11 mandates four-digit `0001`…`0020`. They disagree on content — two-digit `ADR-03` is "Use SQLite
  as the local store", four-digit `0003` is "Adopt Avalonia + .NET LTS + MVVM" — so a citation is
  ambiguous unless the reader already knows which document it came from.
- **`25-ADR` §10 contradicts its own §11.** §10 maps `0020`→"no MVP" and `0014`→"DCO"; §11 says
  `0017`→"No MVP", `0018`→"DCO", and `0014`→"Plugin manifests MUST be signed".

## Format note

`0001` is in the plain Nygard/`adr-tools` layout (a `Date:` line and four `##` sections). `0012` and
`0013` follow the format `25-ADR` §4.3–4.4 actually mandates: an `# NNNN — Title` heading, a
ten-field metadata table, and seven body sections. The two do not match. New ADRs should follow
`25-ADR` §4, since that is the normative document; `0001` is left as written rather than rewritten,
because an ADR is meant to be an immutable record of when a decision was taken.
